what: Nearly three million Teslas recalled in China over hidden door handles

clean_source_blocks.text: Minimalistic door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China's biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles. The recall, which includes 2.98 million Chinese-made Teslas, follows safety concerns that the hidden door handles are difficult to locate and open in emergency situations. Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely. The recalled vehicles will have a warning label stuck on the interior door and receive a software update to automatically lower the windows in a crash. The designs have come under scrutiny after two fatal crashes in China involving Xiaomi EVs, in which power failures were suspected to have prevented doors from being opened.

The action is far bigger than Tesla alone. Tesla and 10 other automakers have recalled nearly 4.3 million vehicles in China over concerns that hidden door handles may be difficult to open in an emergency, according to Reuters. Nine manufacturers, including Tesla, will install warning labels to help occupants identify emergency door releases, while Xiaomi, Xpeng, and Geely brands Zeekr and Lynk & Co are also recalling EVs. Regulators are simultaneously moving to ban the flush-handle design outright, a step no other country has yet taken. Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely.

Tesla said in a statement on Friday that it was recalling some of its Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles due to door handles that are "difficult to identify and operate because their colour is similar to the interior trim". "In extreme situations such as a severe collision causing the vehicle's low-voltage system to fail, this could hinder occupants from quickly opening the doors to escape and impede rescue efforts by those outside the vehicle, posing a safety hazard," it said. Tesla said it would place warning labels on the recalled vehicles and issue a software update to automatically lower a vehicle's windows after a collision. The BBC understands that carmakers have not yet notified authorities of any plans for a similar recall in the US. The BBC has contacted Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely for comment.

[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4g6ggdg030o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
Minimalistic door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China's biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles.

The recall, which includes 2.98 million Chinese-made Teslas, follows safety concerns that the hidden door handles are difficult to locate and open in emergency situations.

Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely.

The recalled vehicles will have a warning label stuck on the interior door and receive a software update to automatically lower the windows in a crash.

The designs have come under scrutiny after two fatal crashes in China involving Xiaomi EVs, in which power failures were suspected to have prevented doors from being opened.

Tesla said in a statement on Friday that it was recalling some of its Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles due to door handles that are "difficult to identify and operate because their colour is similar to the interior trim".

"In extreme situations such as a severe collision causing the vehicle's low-voltage system to fail, this could hinder occupants from quickly opening the doors to escape and impede rescue efforts by those outside the vehicle, posing a safety hazard," it said.

Tesla said it would place warning labels on the recalled vehicles and issue a software update to automatically lower a vehicle's windows after a collision.

The BBC understands that carmakers have not yet notified authorities of any plans for a similar recall in the US.

The BBC has contacted Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely for comment.

The use of hidden handle designs has "snowballed" after Chinese brands were quick to copy the "sleek" look of Tesla's Model S sedan since 2014, said Tu Le, the managing director of consultancy Sino Auto Insights.

The use of warning labels and a software update is more of a "band-aid" than a lasting solution for the issue, he added.

In February, Chinese authorities announced a ban on hidden door handles.

Under new rules due to take effect on 1 January 2027, cars will only be allowed to be sold in China if they have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of their doors.

Tesla's door handles were also involved in a probe by US safety regulators after reports that they suddenly stopped working, leaving children trapped in the cars.

In July, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration suggested creating a new formal safety standard for all carmakers.

[Lähde: YAHOO! | URL: https://autos.yahoo.com/safety-and-recalls/articles/tesla-recalls-3-million-cars-092257914.html]
Tesla has issued a massive recall for its cars in China, but it wasn't alone.

On Monday, the company recalled 2,975,910 vehicles in the country over Tesla's emergency mechanical door release, which the Chinese regulator found difficult to identify and operate.

Tesla vehicles have flush door handles on the outside, and are opened by pressing a button from the inside, but there's an additional mechanical release latch within the car door that opens it in case of emergency. However, China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) found that this latch matches the color of the interior trim too closely, potentially making it hard to find in an emergency.

In total, 973,156 China-built Model 3s, and 1,956,713 Model Ys were recalled, alongside 35,590 imported Model 3s, 8,328 imported Model Xs, and 2,123 imported Model S vehicles.

Other car manufacturers including Xiaomi, Xpeng, and Geely issued recalls for similar issues in their cars as well.

This is Tesla's largest recall in China, but it won't be as costly as it appears. The company plans to solve it with warning labels, as well as an over-the-air update that makes the car's windows lower automatically after a collision.

Additionally and separately, Tesla issued a recall for over 2 million cars in China over inadequate driver monitoring. SAMR found that Tesla's system of checking whether the driver holds the wheel is insufficient, requiring instead that Teslas also track the driver's eyes. This is a solution that Tesla already implements in some models and markets, and will be remedied with a software update.

This recall covers a total of 2,740,642 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, all manufactured in China.

Tesla's door handles were the subject of a probe in the U.S. following reports that door handles in several Model Ys stopped working, leaving children trapped in the cars. It's unclear whether Tesla plans to issue any sort of recall related to the door handles globally.

China has ordered Tesla to recall nearly 3 million vehicles over door handles that safety regulators say could trap occupants inside a crashed car, in what is now the largest automotive recall in the country's history.

China's State Administration for Market Regulation said Friday that Tesla would recall 973,156 Model 3 vehicles built between March 2019 and April 2026, roughly 1.96 million China-made Model Y cars, and thousands of imported Model 3, Model X and Model S units, a total recall of about 2.98 million vehicles, Tesla's largest ever in any market.

The action is far bigger than Tesla alone. Tesla and 10 other automakers have recalled nearly 4.3 million vehicles in China over concerns that hidden door handles may be difficult to open in an emergency, according to Reuters. Nine manufacturers, including Tesla, will install warning labels to help occupants identify emergency door releases, while Xiaomi, Xpeng, and Geely brands Zeekr and Lynk & Co are also recalling EVs. Regulators are simultaneously moving to ban the flush-handle design outright, a step no other country has yet taken.
